key_insight: Staged closure learning trades moderately higher error for substantially fewer model evaluations and more robust optimization than embedded training.
engineering_relevance: Learning closures offline from assimilated trajectories can reduce training costs for dynamical simulators with unresolved effects.
method: Compare embedded closure training with a staged data-assimilation approach.
Infer state and closure trajectories from observations, then train the staged closure offline.
Evaluate both approaches on a synthetic epidemiological SIQR model with a nonlinear, state-dependent quarantine closure.
evidence_signal: In the synthetic SIQR evaluation, embedded training achieved the strongest average accuracy, while staged learning retained comparable qualitative behavior with moderately higher error and substantially fewer model evaluations.
watch_item: Results come from one synthetic exemplar; the accuracy–efficiency trade-off may differ for other systems or observation conditions.
paper_title: Efficient Closure Learning in Dynamical Systems: A Comparison of Data-Assimilated and Embedded Approaches
